summary: Reviewed tools/ci/retry.js diff and tests/ci/retry.reap.test.ts. The privileged sink is unchanged: spawnSync('sudo', ['-n','kill','-s',<name>,'--','-<pid>']) with no shell, signal names from a fixed internal set, pid from child.pid (never from CLI args, env, or files), so there is no injection path. The change only narrows when sudo runs. stopGroup now checks groupExists right before sudo. reap escalates only after two refused kills in a row. Both shrink the PGID-reuse window: the remaining risk is a reuse in the gap between two syscalls on a CI runner, with no attacker-controlled input, so it is not a finding. The new SIGINT/SIGTERM path (stopGroup + shared reapOnce) is bounded: reap has a 2 s deadline and each sudo call has a 10 s spawnSync timeout. A repeat signal is ignored but cannot hang the helper forever, and the runner's SIGKILL still applies. When current is undefined (between attempts) nothing is signalled. When the group is already gone, killGroup returns 'gone' and sudo is not called. On cancel the helper exits even if the reap fails. That matches the old behaviour of exit-on-signal and does not weaken any check. No secrets, no new dependencies, no new untrusted input. No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.
